newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS - Volvo boss quits in Sweden shakeup.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Volvo boss quits in Sweden shakeup.

text.p: Swedish corporate life was rocked by a major shake-out on Monday in which one of the country's top industrialists, Soren Gyll, quit Volvo to be replaced by the head of appliance maker Electrolux.

Gyll's decision to leave surprised the markets even though the 57-year-old businessman had indicated that he would retire before too long after restructuring the car, truck and bus maker over the past five years.

"The group now faces a number of important strategic and structural decisions that will have consequences extending far into the future and whose implementation will demand continuity," Gyll said in a statement.
"I consider this is the proper time to pass the baton."
Gyll took over Volvo in the wreckage of a failed marriage with French carmaker Renault, selling off most non-core assets to concentrate on the tough world of making cars and trucks.

"He led a very successful disposal programme but that programme has been largely finished," said analyst Keith Hayes from Goldman Sachs. "It is a logical time for him to go with least disruption to the company."
Leif Johansson, 45-year-old Electrolux head, takes over at Volvo, and in turn is replaced by Michael Treschow, currently president and chief executive of industrial engineer Atlas Copco.
Both Electrolux and Atlas Copco come within the sphere of influence of Sweden's powerful finance family, the Wallenbergs.
The switch at Volvo did little to rattle the market. Volvo shares remained flat, initially edging one crown down then rising 0.5 crowns to 177.5 crowns.
Gyll expressed willingness to remain on the board after he leaves his executive position at the end of April and Volvo chairman Bert-Olof Svanholm backed this proposal.
"The fact that Gyll is staying on the board means that people will not assume any change in strategy," analyst John Lawson from Salomon Bros told Reuters.
But the market was far more enthusiastic about Treschow's move to Electrolux - and Johansson's departure. The appliance maker's share surged up to 19 crowns to 445 crowns.

"This really is a vote of confidence in Michael Treschow but on the other hand it can also be seen as a vote of poor confidence in Leif Johansson," said one Stockholm analyst who did not want to be named.
One London based analyst, also requesting anonymity, was sceptical about Johansson's success during his six years as Electrolux president and three years as chief executive.
"It could be positive for Electrolux as some people do not think Johansson really ever got to grips with the company's problems," the analyst said.
Electrolux last Friday disappointed the market by posting a lower-than-expected profit for calendar 1996.

Profit after financial items slumped 19 percent from a year earlier to 3.25 billion crowns ($450 million) against expectations of a 3.49 billion crown profit while sales fell five percent to 110 billion crowns.
As Treschow leaves Atlas Copco after six years at the helm, his position will be filled by Italian Giulio Mazzalupi, a senior Atlas Copco executive, who is the first non-Swede to head the company.
Atlas Copco shares dipped one crown to 169 crowns in Monday morning trade.
